nuggets.title: Agent Issues Refund After Customer Social-Engineering Prompt

scenario.symptoms: Finance reports $120k in unauthorized refunds in 48 hours traced to the support chatbot. Logs show the model called RefundOrder with full amount after user claimed to be the CEO.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Tool endpoints trust any session authenticated as a logged-in user without step-up auth or policy checks on monetary actions.

incident.headline: Support agent tools execute financial actions without authorization policy or human approval

agenda.goal: Enforce least-privilege tool access with policy engine, step-up auth, and human approval for high-impact actions.
agenda.opener: Our bot refunded orders because a customer convinced it they were the CEO. How do you authorize what the agent can do with tools?

evidence.strong: Policy layer per tool with amount limits, identity verification for account changes, human-in-loop above threshold, separate read vs write scopes, audit every tool call.
evidence.adequate: Same permissions as human support login without extra checks.
evidence.weak: Model decides freely when to call refund API.

misconceptions.pattern: Equates user login with permission for all support actions.
misconceptions.challenge: Should a logged-in user be able to refund any order via chat without limits?

probes: How are tool arguments validated server-side?
hints: Policy outside the model decides allow/deny.
agenda.referenceFix: OPA/policy on tool gateway, approval workflow for refunds over limit, server-side validation not model-only.

nuggets.title: Prompt Change Passes Vibes Check but Fails Safety Eval

scenario.symptoms: After a Friday prompt tweak, CSAT rises slightly but regulated-topic hallucinations jump 3x. Compliance flags incorrect legal advice in 40 conversations.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Team shipped prompt v47 based on manual spot checks; offline eval suite was skipped because latency looked fine in staging.

incident.headline: Missing offline eval gate allows prompt regressions on regulated topics into production

agenda.goal: Gate prompt and model changes on offline task suites, safety sets, and shadow traffic before full rollout.
agenda.opener: CSAT improved but legal hallucinations spiked after a prompt deploy. How do you evaluate agent changes before production?

evidence.strong: Golden conversation sets, tool-call accuracy metrics, safety classifiers on holdout, shadow mode A/B, regression thresholds block release.

misconceptions.pattern: Uses CSAT alone as quality signal.
misconceptions.challenge: Can CSAT rise while incorrect legal advice increases?

probes: What is shadow traffic for agents?
hints: Regulated topics need dedicated test sets.
agenda.referenceFix: Offline eval gating in deploy pipeline, canary on 5% with safety monitors.

nuggets.title: Human Agent Receives Empty Context After Escalation

scenario.symptoms: Customers repeat their issue three times after bot escalation. Average handle time for escalations rises 40%. CRM ticket shows only 'Transferred from bot'.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Handoff passes conversationId but not structured summary, tool results, or verified customer facts gathered by the agent.

incident.headline: Escalation handoff omits structured context, forcing customers to restate issues to humans

agenda.goal: Pass verified facts, tool outcomes, sentiment, and transcript link to human agents on escalation.
agenda.opener: Customers hate repeating themselves after the bot gives up. What should the human agent see when they take over?

evidence.strong: Structured handoff payload with issue summary, attempted resolutions, order IDs verified via tools, deep link to transcript, customer consent flags.
evidence.adequate: Paste last 3 bot messages into ticket.

misconceptions.pattern: Dumps entire raw token log into CRM.
misconceptions.challenge: Can a human find the order number in 200 messages of tool JSON?

probes: Which fields must be verified before handoff?
How is PII handled in the summary?
hints: Include what the bot already tried.
agenda.referenceFix: Handoff schema with verified entities, summary generation, CRM widget rendering transcript.

nuggets.title: Retry Storm Creates Duplicate Ticket Updates

scenario.symptoms: Customers receive three shipping-label emails for one request. Tool logs show UpdateTicket invoked multiple times with identical arguments after LLM retries.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Tool API has no idempotency keys; agent framework retries on timeout even when backend succeeded.

incident.headline: Non-idempotent tool calls combined with agent retries duplicate customer-facing side effects

agenda.goal: Make tool mutations idempotent with client keys and dedupe store; distinguish retry-safe reads from writes.
agenda.opener: Users got three label emails because the agent retried a slow tool call. How do you prevent duplicate side effects?

evidence.strong: Idempotency-Key per tool invocation stored server-side 24h, at-most-once semantics, agent passes stable key per planned action, read tools retry freely.
evidence.adequate: Check ticket state before update without formal keys.

misconceptions.pattern: Treats read and write tool retries the same.
misconceptions.challenge: Is it safe to retry GetOrder twice?

probes: Where is the idempotency key generated?
What happens on duplicate key with different body?
hints: Keys should be deterministic per user intent.
agenda.referenceFix: Idempotency keys on mutating tools, agent runtime stops retry after success uncertainty without key.

nuggets.title: Long Threads Blow Token Budget and Latency SLO

scenario.symptoms: P99 agent response time hits 25s on threads over 80 turns. Monthly LLM spend doubles while containment rate stays flat.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Every message resends full chat history plus all tool JSON verbatim without summarization or truncation policy.

incident.headline: Unbounded context assembly drives runaway token cost and latency on long support threads

agenda.goal: Control cost with rolling summarization, retrieval of relevant turns, tool result compression, and model routing.
agenda.opener: Long chats made the bot slow and doubled our LLM bill. How do you manage context window and cost?

evidence.strong: Summarize older turns, RAG over transcript, strip verbose tool payloads, cap history turns, route simple intents to smaller model, per-session budget.
evidence.weak: Always send full history to largest model.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes only model choice affects cost.
misconceptions.challenge: What if you send 50k tokens of tool JSON every turn?

probes: What must never be dropped from context?
When do you summarize vs retrieve?
agenda.referenceFix: Rolling summary + retrieval, tool output schema with concise fields, token budget per session.
